site.heroCaption: EXHIBIT 0: The trail. Twelve things on a list, and one man wearing most of them. Click a pin. Click a stripe. LOOK.
intro: This is the packing list. Not the picture, the LIST: printed in the white margin, in capitals, by a man who tells you his name before he tells you anything else.

Night 35. The beach took thirty-one of them. This hike took one, because this time he wrote it all down. Somewhere around 4 AM I stopped asking WHO he is and started counting what he carries. ==Twelve items.== ==One man.==
Every proof below has a SEE FOR YOURSELF button. I'm not asking you to trust me. I'm asking you to READ IT. ~~I'm not crazy.~~ Just read it.
Start with the first line. It always starts with the first line. (Same as the beach postcard: the name comes first.)
site.censusInstructions: Click every striped thing in the scene above.

claims.title: HE SAYS HIS NAME, THEN HE PUTS ON THE HAT

facts.text: The letter in the margin says: "MY NAME IS WALDO."
The figure above the letter wears a red-and-white bobble hat and round glasses.

claims.leap: A man who gives you his name and puts on the hat in the same breath is not introducing himself. He is being ==issued==. A name and a hat that arrive together are a uniform with a name tag.

update.text: I read the first line nine times. MY NAME IS WALDO. Then I looked at the hat. Then I looked at the hat again. CONVENIENT.

claims.note: HE INTRODUCED HIMSELF WITH A HAT
claims.alt: The complete Waldo figure: red-and-white bobble hat, round glasses, striped shirt, blue jeans, walking stick and cup, above the letter.
claims.caption: his name, his hat, his stick.

links.label: THE LIST THAT COMES WITH HIM

claims.title: THE KIT IS COMPLETE. ONE MAN IS WEARING IT.

facts.text: The letter lists twelve things he says he has: walking stick, kettle, mallet, cup, backpack, sleeping bag, binoculars, camera, snorkel, belt, bag and shovel.
The complete Waldo carries a cup, a walking stick and a backpack, with a rolled bundle strapped on top.

claims.leap: Twelve items on one list, and the man who signed it is carrying most of them at once. A packing list that fits one body this exactly is not a packing list. It's an ==issue sheet==. Nobody gets issued a whole kit. Except him.

update.text: I counted the list. Twelve. Then I counted what he is carrying, and it kept matching the list. Who packs for a hike and fits the whole thing to one man?

claims.alt: The packing list in the margin: walking stick, kettle, mallet, cup, backpack, sleeping bag, binoculars, camera, snorkel, belt, bag and shovel.
claims.caption: twelve items. one body.

claims.title: TWENTY-FIVE WATCHERS FOR ONE OUTFIT

facts.text: The letter says there are "ALSO 25 WALDO-WATCHERS SOMEWHERE."
This lookalike wears a bobble hat, a striped top and a blue skirt. No jeans.

claims.leap: Twenty-five people whose whole job is to watch for him. You don't post twenty-five watchers for one man. You post them for an outfit that ==keeps changing shape==. Look at the skirt: same hat, same stripes, new cut. That's what they're watching for.

update.text: I have now pictured twenty-five watchers. Every one of them was looking at the skirt.

claims.alt: A lookalike in a red-and-white bobble hat, striped top, blue skirt and striped stockings, at the bottom middle of the scene.
claims.caption: same hat. new skirt.

claims.title: THE MARCH: SAME STEP, SAME DIRECTION

facts.text: The letter says each of the 25 watchers appears "ONLY ONCE IN MY TRAVELS."
Two printed rows of striped walkers under the letter, most of them in bobble hats and most heading the same way.

claims.leap: Twenty-five watchers, each turning up once and then gone. The walkers printed right under the letter do the opposite: most of them walk the same stride in the same direction. Watchers scatter. Uniforms march. ==One set of instructions does that.==

update.text: Closed the curtains. The rows are still marching in my head. Left foot. Left foot. CONVENIENT.

claims.alt: Two rows of striped walkers in red-and-white bobble hats, most walking in the same direction.
claims.caption: left foot, left foot.

claims.title: LINE THEM UP. EVERY ONE IS MISSING A PIECE.

facts.text: The blond lookalike wears a red-and-white hat, with yellow hair showing beneath it.
The glasses lookalike has a bobble hat, round glasses and blue jeans, but no walking stick.

claims.leap: Four suspects, and every one is missing something: a stick, a backpack, or the jeans. None of them is the whole kit. The kit isn't a person. It is a set of parts that someone keeps ==handing out==.

update.text: I drew this lineup on the back of a receipt. Four faces. Four missing pieces. I checked twice.

claims.alt: Four lookalikes in one strip: each wears some of the outfit and is missing other pieces.
claims.caption: four suspects. no full set.

links.label: THE SKIRT IS IN THE LINEUP

claims.title: ODLAW WEARS THE STRIPES IN THE WRONG COLOURS

facts.text: Odlaw wears black-and-yellow stripes, a black hat and black trousers.
The letter asks: "AND ODLAW'S BINOCULARS?"

claims.leap: Odlaw has stripes too. Yellow instead of red and white. The letter asks where his binoculars are, and the binoculars are on the list. ==Same kit, reversed, issued to the other side.==

update.text: Opposite stripes. Same cut. Two sets, one for each side, and one of them is in the wrong colours on purpose.

claims.alt: Odlaw in black-and-yellow stripes, a black hat and black trousers, walking across the lower left of the scene.
claims.caption: the other set.

links.label: THE BINOCULARS ARE ON THE LIST

claims.title: THE MAN ON THE LEDGE IS WATCHING THE STRIPES

facts.text: A man sits on the ledge with a dark object raised to his face.
A red-and-white striped awning runs into the red-brick wall just to his left.

claims.leap: He is up on the brick wall beside the awning, with something to his eye, and the list has binoculars on it. ==Nobody watches a street that closely unless they were told what to look for.==

update.text: The ledge is the one spot on the street nobody can reach from the ground. I checked. I didn't go up.

claims.alt: A man sits on a ledge beside a red-and-white awning, with a dark object raised to his face.
claims.caption: lookout. striped awning below.

claims.title: THE PROPS CHANGE HANDS

facts.text: The letter says the camera is Wenda's, and the scroll belongs to Wizard Whitebeard.
Wizard Whitebeard holds a staff striped in red, white and blue.

claims.leap: The camera on his list is Wenda's. The scroll is the wizard's. Every prop on the list has another owner, and the wizard is holding a striped pole. ==Stripes are what the props are dressed in.==

update.text: I can't find the camera. I can find the staff. The staff is striped. The camera is a rumour.

claims.alt: Wizard Whitebeard in a red robe and blue pointed hat, holding a red, white and blue striped staff.
claims.caption: the props have new owners.

claims.title: HE SIGNED THE SEARCH

facts.text: A handwritten "Waldo" with a scribbled underline sits just past the end of the letter's last printed line.
The printed line beside it ends "...A SEARCH!"

claims.leap: He wrote his name just past the word SEARCH, the way you sign for a delivery. Waldo is not the one looking. ==Waldo is what you sign for.==

update.text: He signed it. Nobody signs a crowd unless they want the credit. CONVENIENT.

claims.alt: Handwritten Waldo with a scribbled underline beside a line of printed text ending in A SEARCH.
claims.caption: he signed the search.

claims.title: EVEN THE DOG IS IN UNIFORM

facts.text: The letter names the dog: "WOOF (BUT ALL YOU CAN SEE IS HIS TAIL)."
The dog wears a red-and-white hat, and his body and tail are striped.

claims.leap: The letter names the dog and then tells you what you can see of him. What you can see is a hat and stripes, body and tail, all in the same uniform. ==He was dressed for the page, like everyone else.==

update.text: The dog is in the same uniform as the rest of them, and nobody in the letter asks why. Think about it.

claims.alt: A dog in a red-and-white hat with a striped body and striped tail, on the lower middle of the scene.
claims.caption: all you can see.

censusComments: Fourteen stripes so far. Four of them are on the people with the hat. I did not expect that.
The café awning is red and white. Odlaw's shirt is black and yellow. Same cut, wrong colours. I've written it down twice.
The wizard's staff is stripes too. Even the pole is in uniform. Nobody told the pole.
UPDATE 5:52 AM: The blue awning in the market is not red and white. It counts anyway. Stripes are stripes.
Still counting. The more I look, the more I find. That's how you know it's the pattern.

guestbook.name: kestrel_mom_22
guestbook.text: It's a camping list. Waldo has a stick and a cup. You're reading a children's book like it's a file.
guestbook.reply: Kestrel. The list says "I'VE GOT ALL I NEED." Read it again, then count what he is carrying.

guestbook.name: gridlock_ben
guestbook.text: Odlaw is just the bad guy. Black and yellow is a bee. That's the whole theory.
guestbook.reply: A bee is also a uniform. ~~I'm not crazy.~~ Bees don't have binoculars. Odlaw's are on the list.

guestbook.name: nope_nope_nope
guestbook.text: So there are 25 different men? Why would anyone make 25 men?
guestbook.reply: Nobody said 25 men. The letter said 25 Waldo-watchers. Those are not men. Ask the skirt.

updates.text: I scanned the letter forty times. Every line reads like an intro. None of them reads like a name tag. CONVENIENT.
The list is printed, not handwritten. Printed means issued. I called the office that prints things. Nobody there has heard of Waldo.
The watcher on the ledge hasn't moved in my notes. I have not looked away from him. Not once.
The dog is striped from the body to the tail, and nobody in the letter asks why. Think about it.
The walker strip under this letter is the scroll's strip. Same rows. Same Odlaw. Same wizard. Same 25 WALDO-WATCHERS. Not similar. THE SAME. You don't reprint a man. You reprint a catalogue.

receipts.note: NOT ORDERED BY ME. "I'VE GOT ALL I NEED."
one per watcher, each seen once

receipts.item: Black pen, used on a search

lines: He says his name is Waldo. He says it on a list of twelve things, and the man who signed it is carrying most of them.
Twenty-five watchers, each seen once, all watching one outfit. Four suspects, and none of them is complete.
The only complete kit is on the man who signed the search. Everyone else is wearing a piece of it, and the stripes are handed out to the rest.
